clue.text: Stripped of crown, old King put back in King's birthplace

indicators.note: losing a crown means losing the top, so the first letter of the old king's name goes
putting something back sends it the other way, so the joined letters are read from the end

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme, without his first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deposed old monarch is returned to the town where the King was born.
explanation.walkthrough: The King of the definition is Elvis Presley, born in this Mississippi town; the old king of the wordplay is Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme, who loses his C.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley, called the King of rock and roll, was born in this Mississippi town.

clue.text: Green tea brewed for Joan of Arc when executed?

indicators.note: brewed tea has been stirred up in the pot, so the letters are churned

parts.note: all eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A cup of herbal brew made for a martyred French saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Joan of Arc was burned at the stake aged nineteen, so the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: She was nineteen at her death, an age within the thirteen-to-nineteen span of adolescence.

clue.text: Where Rick played softly, bit of solid gold

parts.note: piano is the musical term for soft
a bar of gold is an ingot

explanation.surface: A musician performed quietly, a golden moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Rick is the café owner of the film Casablanca, where Sam plays piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge with live keyboard music, like Rick's Café Américain, is this kind of venue.

clue.text: Removing cap, splash in mud where Oddfellows gather

indicators.note: taking off a cap removes the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: to plodge is a dialect word meaning to wade or splash through mud or water

explanation.surface: Take off your hat before wading through the mire to the members' meeting hall.
explanation.walkthrough: PLODGE is a northern English dialect verb, to wade.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oddfellows, a fraternal society like the Freemasons, meet in local branches each called by this name.

clue.text: Women covering courts to show sports logos

indicators.note: one thing covering another wraps around it, so the women's letters go outside

parts.note: she's, plural of she, a female person
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: Female players are draped over tennis courts to display the brand marks of sportswear firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' looks like tennis courts but is the verb meaning romances.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nike tick is called a swoosh, so these curved brand marks on athletic gear are examples.

clue.text: Forgoing competition, saving time, leaving no evidence

indicators.note: saving something keeps it held safe within, so the time letter goes inside

parts.note: without a race, going without a contest
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A runner skips the contest to save time and covers their tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that vanishes this way leaves nothing behind to show it was ever there, an idiom.

clue.text: Blue, rotten apricot or salmon?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a bad shade, apricot and salmon being names of colours

explanation.walkthrough: Apricot and salmon look like fruit and fish going off, but they are pinkish-orange colours, and a poor one is literally off.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue joke is a smutty one, which is also called risqué or in poor taste.

clue.text: Odist's dance at church

parts.note: the hora is a Jewish and Balkan circle dance
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A poet goes dancing in a church hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman poet famous for his Odes is a writer of lyric poems.

clue.text: Cleo's killer beheaded on this spot in field

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the snake is removed

parts.note: Cleopatra died by the bite of an asp, here without its first letter
here means in this place

explanation.surface: The snake that killed Cleopatra was decapitated right here in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: An area of activity or expertise, like a field of study, is also called a sphere of influence.

clue.text: Horny beast seen in much of Auld Sod

indicators.note: much of something is most but not all of it, so some letters are dropped

parts.note: the Auld Sod is a sentimental name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A horned animal spotted roaming across most of the old country.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two letters, IR, are dropped from IRELAND.
explanation.definitionFit: This large African antelope has long spiral horns, making it a horned animal.

clue.text: Proposes factions come before Yank's holiday in report

parts.note: sets are groups of like-minded people

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the holiday's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: the Fourth of July, the American national holiday

explanation.surface: Political groups put forward ideas ahead of an American Independence Day celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Yank is both the setter and an American, whose holiday is the Fourth (of July).
explanation.definitionFit: To set forth a plan is to present or put it forward for consideration, the same as proposing.

clue.text: Fixing craps game, I'm an employer of dirty tricks

indicators.note: fixing a game means rigging it, so the letters are tampered with

parts.note: all thirteen letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked gambler boasts of rigging a dice game with underhand tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: Craps is an American dice game.
explanation.definitionFit: A political drive to blacken an opponent's name relies on underhand methods and false rumours.

clue.text: Positive on location of closing parenthesis?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: greater than nothing, as a number or temperature
second meaning: where the ) key sits on a keyboard, over the digit 0

explanation.walkthrough: On a standard keyboard the closing bracket is the shifted character on the key whose main character is the digit nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers greater than nothing are positive, and the bracket symbol is printed over the nought key.

clue.text: It arrives after November and it's 13½ inches tall

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the next code word in the NATO phonetic alphabet
second meaning: the Academy Award statuette, which stands that high

explanation.walkthrough: November is not the month but the NATO radio code word for N; the following letter O is signalled with this word.
explanation.definitionFit: In the radio spelling alphabet O follows N, and the film award statuette measures thirteen and a half inches.

clue.text: Worry former partner with messy separation

indicators.note: a messy thing is jumbled up, so the letters of the following word are muddled

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
all ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Fretting over an ex because of an untidy break-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names an anxious, irritated state of mind, close in sense to the noun for fretting.

clue.text: Not much money for pair of singers

parts.note: Tom Petty, American rock singer
Johnny Cash, American country singer

explanation.surface: A duet act gets paid very little.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair of singers are Tom Petty and Johnny Cash.
explanation.definitionFit: An office keeps a small fund of coins and notes for minor expenses, a modest sum.

clue.text: Underworld hack rejected secretive body part

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word for the horse is read the other way

parts.note: a hack is a worn-out horse, a nag
a gland secretes, a pun on secretive

explanation.surface: A journalist turned down for a story about a shadowy organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests a reporter, but means an old horse; 'secretive' is read as secreting.
explanation.definitionFit: The world of organised crime and its gangsters is called the criminal underworld.

clue.text: Figuratively, Olive Oyl, head Bialystok resident?

parts.note: bean is slang for the head
Bialystok is a city in Poland

explanation.surface: A cartoon girlfriend is introduced as the leader of a Polish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Olive Oyl is Popeye's very tall, thin girlfriend in the cartoons.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall skinny person is called this, after the long sticks gardeners use to support climbing plants.

clue.text: Interest expressed by two sailors at sea, shelled fare

indicators.note: something expressed is spoken, so the word for interest is taken by its sound

parts.note: a stake is a financial interest in something
a tar is a sailor, so two of them

indicators.note: a shelled thing has lost its outer casing, so only the middle letter of the word for sea is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pair of seamen at sea shelling something to eat, with money at stake.
explanation.definitionFit: This raw minced beef dish is a kind of food or menu item, which is what fare means.

clue.text: Operatic villain, maybe little green man, one with big ears

parts.note: villains in opera are often sung by a bass
ET, the alien of the film

explanation.surface: A cast list: a stage baddie, a space alien, and a creature with huge ears.
explanation.definitionFit: This short-legged hunting hound is known for its long drooping lobes either side of its head.

clue.text: Doctor issued cause of atrophy

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

parts.note: all six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician has handed out an explanation for wasting muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscles and organs that go unused waste away, so lack of use leads to wasting.

clue.text: Coolidge escapes catastrophe for peace

indicators.note: the president escaping means his nickname leaves the longer word

parts.note: a calamity is a disaster
Calvin Coolidge, US president, was known as Cal

explanation.surface: A president flees a disaster in search of tranquillity.
explanation.walkthrough: Calvin Coolidge, 30th US president, went by Silent Cal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations between people or nations, a state of harmony and goodwill.

clue.text: Penny, a migrant, healed bird

indicators.note: what is healed is restored and put back together, so these letters are re-formed

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny
all eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A wounded traveller is nursed back to health, with a coin involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent P of the answer comes from the penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouse of mountain and arctic regions that turns white in winter is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Athlete coming from rear in preliminaries

indicators.note: coming from the rear means read from back to front
in shows the letters sit inside the longer word that follows

parts.note: the second to sixth letters

explanation.surface: A runner charges through from the back during the qualifying heats.
explanation.definitionFit: A middle-distance runner who specialises in the one-mile race is a kind of track athlete.

clue.text: Seek treasure perhaps in small island, shady place

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the Caribbean island
a dive is a disreputable bar or club

explanation.surface: Hunting for buried riches on a tiny island in some disreputable spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shady' suggests shade from the sun, but means disreputable.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwater swimmers with breathing tanks often explore wrecks, so searching for sunken riches is one example.

clue.text: Section of Villanova, home to vaqueros

indicators.note: a section is a piece cut from within a longer word

parts.note: the third to seventh letters

explanation.surface: Part of a Pennsylvania university campus houses Mexican cowboys.
explanation.walkthrough: Villanova is a US university; vaqueros are Spanish-American cowboys.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a grassy plain of Latin America where cattle are herded by mounted cowhands.

clue.text: Chewing on something hard: golf ball?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a baby does when its first molars and incisors come through
second meaning: split as ..., a thing set on a tee

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning only works split into two words: a golf ball is the thing you place on a tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies cutting their first molars and incisors gnaw on hard rings and toys to soothe their gums.

clue.text: Game canine evacuated, cutting cheese

indicators.note: a knife cutting cheese goes into it, so these letters sit inside the cheese

parts.note: the soft French cheese

indicators.note: an evacuated place has been emptied, so the inside of the dog's name goes

parts.note: a canine is a dog

explanation.surface: A hound, with no stomach for the game, attacks a wedge of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: DOG loses its middle letter O to give DG, which goes into BRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a trick-taking card game for four players in two partnerships.
